title: standardize GPU init lifecycle and introduce layered compatibility adapters
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: We still observe sporadic cold-start stalls and inconsistent kernel selection across heterogeneous fleets when upgrading CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS stacks. Root causes include ad-hoc init ordering, fragile probe fallbacks, and multiple places that assume legacy CUTLASS symbol names and memory alignment behavior. This ticket will consolidate the GPU initialization lifecycle into a single, observable sequence and introduce a layered compatibility adapter pattern that isolates model-serving code from direct assumptions about kernel symbols or ABI details.

Goals:
- Create a single GPU init coordinator responsible for capability detection, kernel feature negotiation, and warmup orchestration.
- Implement a compatibility adapter layer: a thin, versioned adapter per CUTLASS/Triton/CUDA family that translates runtime capabilities into normalized feature flags used by the serving runtime.
- Eliminate duplicated probe logic in at least 3 subsystems (quant loader, kernel scheduler, runtime warmup) by routing them through the coordinator.
- Add guarded rollback hooks to allow safe live downgrade of kernel adapter mappings when a regression is detected.
- Improve observability: emit events for each init step, probe metric, and adapter selection decision (to Console tracing and runtime logs).

Non-goals: Full CUTLASS refactor or reimplementing kernels. This is an orchestration and compatibility surface cleanup only.
acceptance_criteria: All GPU init/probe logic consolidated behind the GPU init coordinator and removed from quant loader/kernel scheduler/warmup modules.
Compatibility adapters implemented for the current CUTLASS and Triton versions we run (see links) and feature-negotiation tests added.
No increase in median cold-start latency across a staging fleet; P95 cold-start latency reduced by at least 15% in staging benchmarks.
Automated rollback hook allows mapping changes without container restarts in at least one canary cluster.
New init/tracing events surface in Console runtime-1.20 dashboard and are included in token-level trace samples for debugging.
risks: Incorrect capability translation could cause subtle performance regressions for quantized kernels.
Adapter bugs could lead to failed kernel loads on specific GPU models not present in CI fleet.
Live rollback primitives introduce complexity and could interfere with autoscaler if not rate-limited.
implementation_plan: Design: finalize coordinator API and adapter interface. (owner: Diego)
Spike: prototype adapter for CUTLASS v3.x to validate translation table and tests (owner: Priya Shah).
Refactor: extract probe logic into coordinator; wire quant loader and scheduler to call coordinator (owner: runtime team).
Compat layer: implement adapter registry, version negotiation, and loading semantics with explicit fallbacks (owner: runtime infra).
Observability: add structured init events and Console mapping; ensure events are sampled and have low overhead.
Testing: add unit tests for translation tables, integration tests on staging heterogeneous fleet, and long-running soak with synthetic workload.
Rollout: canary deploy to 5% of serving capacity with automatic perf checks; hold/backout criteria defined.
testing_plan: Unit: adapter interface contract tests and mock probe responses.
Integration: run on heterogeneous staging nodes with mixed GPU generations; verify kernel selection matrix matches expectations.
Perf: cold-start benchmark harness comparing baseline vs coordinator on 1000 startup samples.
Safety: chaos test that simulates partial adapter load failures and validates rollback path.
